cues.zh: 本视频的部分内容由 LastPass 赞助。

cues.en: This video is about a pattern people thought was impossible
cues.zh: 本期视频要讲一种曾被认为不可能存在的图案，

cues.en: and a material that wasn't supposed to exist.
cues.zh: 以及一种理应不存在的材料。

cues.en: The story begins over four hundred years ago in Prague.
cues.zh: 故事始于 400 多年前的布拉格。

cues.en: I'm now in Prague in The Czech Republic, which is perhaps my favorite European city that I've visited so far. I'm going to visit the Kepler Museum because he's one of the most famous scientists who lived and worked around Prague. I want to tell you five things about Johannes Kepler that are essential to our story.
cues.zh: 我现在在捷克的布拉格，这可能是我目前去过的欧洲城市里最喜欢的一座。我正要去参观 Kepler 博物馆，因为他是曾在布拉格生活和工作过的最著名的科学家之一。关于 Johannes Kepler，有五件事对我们接下来的故事至关重要，我想先告诉大家。

cues.en: Number one, Kepler is most famous for figuring out that the shapes of planetary orbits are ellipses.
cues.zh: 第一点，Kepler 最著名的成就，是发现行星轨道其实是椭圆形的。

cues.en: But before he came to this realization,
cues.zh: 但在意识到这一点之前，

cues.en: he invented a model of the solar system in which the planets were on nested spheres
cues.zh: 他曾构想过一个太阳系模型，行星分布在嵌套的球面上，

cues.en: separated by the platonic solids.
cues.zh: 球体之间由柏拉图多面体隔开。

cues.en: What are the platonic solids? Well, they are objects where all of the faces are identical and all of the vertices are identical, which means you can rotate them through some angle and they look the same as they did before.
cues.zh: 什么是柏拉图多面体？简单来说，就是所有面都完全相同、所有顶点也都完全相同的几何体，这意味着无论你旋转多少特定角度，它们看起来都和原来一模一样。

cues.en: So the cube is an obvious example, then you also have the tetrahedron,
cues.zh: 立方体就是一个很典型的例子，此外还有正四面体、

cues.en: the octahedron,
cues.zh: 正八面体、

cues.en: the dodecahedron,
cues.zh: 正十二面体——

cues.en: which has 12 pentagonal sides,
cues.zh: 它由 12 个正五边形面组成，

cues.en: and the icosahedron,
cues.zh: 以及正二十面体——

cues.en: which has 20 sides.
cues.zh: 它有 20 个面。

cues.en: And that's it. There are just five platonic solids,
cues.zh: 就这些了。柏拉图多面体总共就只有这五种，

cues.en: which was convenient for Kepler because in his day, they only knew about six planets.
cues.zh: 这对 Kepler 来说再合适不过了，因为在那个时代，人们总共也只知道六颗行星。

cues.en: So this allowed him to put a unique platonic solid between each of the planetary spheres. Essentially, he used them as spacers.
cues.zh: 于是，这让他能在每两个行星天球之间放入一个独特的柏拉图立体。本质上，他把它们当作间隔物。

cues.en: He carefully selected the order of the platonic solids so that the distances between planets would match astronomical
cues.zh: 他仔细选择柏拉图立体的顺序，让行星之间的距离尽可能匹配天文

cues.en: observations as closely as possible.
cues.zh: 观测结果。

cues.en: He had this deep abiding belief that there was some geometric regularity in the universe.
cues.zh: 他深信宇宙中存在某种几何规律性。

cues.en: And of course, there is, just not this.
cues.zh: 当然，确实有，只不过不是这个。

cues.en: Two.
cues.zh: 第二。

cues.en: Kepler's attraction to geometry extended to more practical questions like, how do you stack cannonballs so they take up the least space on a ship's deck? By 1611, Kepler had an answer. Hexagonal close packing and the face centered cubic arrangement are both equivalently
cues.zh: Kepler 对几何的兴趣延伸到更实际的问题，比如：怎么堆叠炮弹，才能让它们在船甲板上占最少空间？到 1611 年，Kepler 有了答案。六方最密堆积和面心立方排列都等效地

cues.en: and optimally efficient with cannonballs
cues.zh: 并且在炮弹堆积上同样最优高效

cues.en: occupying about 74%
cues.zh: 占据约 74%

cues.en: of the volume they take up. Now this might seem like the obvious way to stack spheres. I mean, is the way that oranges are stacked in the supermarket.
cues.zh: 它们所占的体积。现在这似乎是堆叠球体的显而易见的方式。我是说，就是超市里堆橙子的方式。

cues.en: But Kepler hadn't proved it. He just stated it as fact, which is why this became known as Kepler's conjecture.
cues.zh: 但 Kepler 并没有证明它。他只是把它当作事实陈述出来，所以这被称为 Kepler 猜想。

cues.en: Now it turns out he was right, but it took around four hundred years to prove it. The formal proof was only published in the journal Form of Mathematics in 2017.
cues.zh: 结果发现他是对的，但证明它花了大约四百年。正式证明直到 2017 年才发表在期刊 Form of Mathematics 上。

cues.en: Three, Kepler published his conjecture in a pamphlet called, De Neva Sixangula,
cues.zh: 第三，Kepler 在一本名为 De Neva Sixangula 的小册子中发表了他的猜想，

cues.en: on the six cornered snowflake,
cues.zh: 即关于六角雪花，

cues.en: in which he wondered, there must be a definite cause why whenever snow begins to fall, its initial formations invariably display the shape of a six cornered starlet. For if it happens by chance, why do they not fall just as well with five corners or with seven?
cues.zh: 在书中他思考：每当雪开始飘落，其初始形态总是呈现六角小星形，这背后必定有确定的原因。因为如果是偶然发生，为什么它们不会同样以五角或七角落下呢？

cues.en: Why always with six?
cues.zh: 为什么总是六？

cues.en: In Kepler's day, there was no real theory of atoms or molecules or how they self arrange into crystals. But Kepler seemed to be on the verge of understanding this. I mean, he speculates about the smallest natural unit of a liquid like water, essentially a water molecule,
cues.zh: 在开普勒的时代，还没有真正关于原子、分子或它们如何自组织成晶体的理论。但开普勒似乎快要理解这一点了。我是说，他推测像水这样的液体的最小自然单位，本质上就是一个水分子，

cues.en: and how these tiny units could stack together mechanically to form the hexagonal crystal,
cues.zh: 以及这些微小单位如何机械地堆叠在一起形成六角晶体，

cues.en: not unlike the hexagonal close packed cannonballs.
cues.zh: 就像六角密排的炮弹一样。

cues.en: Four.
cues.zh: 四。

cues.en: Kepler knew that regular hexagons can cover a flat surface perfectly with no gaps. In mathematical jargon, we say the hexagon tiles the plane periodically.
cues.zh: 开普勒知道正六边形可以完美覆盖平面而没有间隙。用数学术语来说，我们说六边形周期性铺砌平面。

cues.en: You know that a tiling is periodic if you can duplicate a portion of it and continue the pattern only through translation
cues.zh: 你知道，如果一个铺砌可以通过平移复制其一部分并继续图案，那么它就是周期性的

cues.en: with no rotations or reflections.
cues.zh: 没有旋转或反射。

cues.en: Periodic tilings can also have rotational symmetry. A rhombus pattern has twofold symmetry because if you rotate it a 180 degrees, one half turn, the pattern looks the same as it did before.
cues.zh: 周期性铺砌也可以具有旋转对称性。菱形图案具有二重对称性，因为如果你将它旋转180度，即半圈，图案看起来和之前一样。

cues.en: Equilateral triangles have threefold symmetry.
cues.zh: 等边三角形具有三重对称性。

cues.en: Squares
cues.zh: 正方形

cues.en: have fourfold symmetry.
cues.zh: 具有四重对称性。

cues.en: And hexagons
cues.zh: 而六边形

cues.en: have sixfold symmetry.
cues.zh: 具有六重对称性。

cues.en: But those are the only symmetries you can have. Two, three, four, and six. There is no fivefold symmetry.
cues.zh: 但这些是你唯一可以拥有的对称性。二、三、四和六。没有五重对称性。

cues.en: Regular pentagons do not tile the plane. But that didn't stop Kepler from trying.
cues.zh: 正五边形不能铺砌平面。但这并没有阻止开普勒尝试。

cues.en: See this pattern right here?
cues.zh: 看到这个图案了吗？

cues.en: He published it in his book Harmonicis Mundi or Harmony of the World.
cues.zh: 他将其发表在他的书《Harmonicis Mundi》或《世界的和谐》中。

cues.en: It has a certain fivefold symmetry,
cues.zh: 它具有一定的五重对称性，

cues.en: but not exactly.
cues.zh: 但并不完全如此。

cues.en: And it's not entirely clear how you would continue this pattern to tile the whole plane.
cues.zh: 而且不太清楚如何延续这个图案来铺满整个平面。

cues.en: There are an infinite number of shapes that can tile the plane periodically.
cues.zh: 有无限多种形状可以周期性铺满平面。

cues.en: The regular hexagon can only tile the plane periodically.
cues.zh: 正六边形只能周期性铺满平面。

cues.en: There are also an infinite number of shapes that can tile the plane periodically or nonperiodically.
cues.zh: 也有无限多种形状可以周期性或非周期性铺满平面。

cues.en: For example, isosceles triangles can tile the plane periodically,
cues.zh: 例如，等腰三角形可以周期性铺满平面，

cues.en: but if you rotate a pair of triangles,
cues.zh: 但如果你旋转一对三角形，

cues.en: well then the pattern is no longer perfectly periodic.
cues.zh: 那么这个图案就不再完全周期性了。

cues.en: A sphinx tile can join with another, rotate it at 180 degrees,
cues.zh: 狮身人面像拼块可以与另一个拼合，将其旋转180度，

cues.en: and tile the plane periodically.
cues.zh: 并周期性铺满平面。

cues.en: But a different arrangement of these same tiles is non periodic.
cues.zh: 但这些相同拼块的另一种排列则是非周期性的。

cues.en: This raises the question, are there some tiles that can only tile the plane non periodically?
cues.zh: 这就引出了一个问题：是否存在某些拼块只能非周期性铺满平面？

cues.en: Well, in 1961,
Hao Wang was studying multicolored
cues.zh: Hao Wang正在研究多色

cues.en: square tiles.
cues.zh: 方形拼块。

cues.en: The rules were touching edges must be the same color and you can't rotate or reflect tiles, only slide them around. Now the question was, if you're given a set of these tiles, can you tell if they will tile the plane?
cues.zh: 规则是接触的边缘必须是相同颜色，并且你不能旋转或反射拼块，只能滑动它们。现在的问题是，如果给你一组这样的拼块，你能判断它们是否能铺满平面吗？

cues.en: Wang's conjecture was that if they can tile the plane, well, they can do so periodically.
cues.zh: Wang的猜想是，如果它们能铺满平面，那么它们可以周期性铺满。

cues.en: But it turned out Wang's conjecture was false.
cues.zh: 但结果证明Wang的猜想是错误的。

cues.en: His student Robert Berger found a set of 20,426
cues.zh: 他的学生Robert Berger找到了一组20,426块

cues.en: tiles that could tile the plane but only non periodically.
cues.zh: 拼块，可以铺满平面但只能非周期性地。

cues.en: Think about that for a second. Here we have a finite set of tiles. Okay. It's a large number, but it's finite and it can tile all the way out to infinity
cues.zh: 想一下这个。这里我们有一组有限的拼块。好吧，这是一个很大的数字，但它是有限的，并且它可以一直铺展到无穷远

cues.en: without ever repeating the same pattern.
cues.zh: 而从不重复相同的图案。

cues.en: There's no way even to force them to tile periodically.
cues.zh: 甚至无法强迫它们周期性铺砌。

cues.en: And a set of tiles like this that can only tile the plane non periodically
cues.zh: 而像这样只能非周期性铺满平面的一组瓷砖

cues.en: is called an aperiodic
cues.zh: 被称为非周期

cues.en: tiling.
cues.zh: 铺砌。

cues.en: And mathematicians
cues.zh: 数学家们

cues.en: wanted to know,
cues.zh: 想知道，

cues.en: were there aperiodic
cues.zh: 是否存在所需的瓷砖

cues.en: tilings that required fewer
cues.zh: 更少的非周期

cues.en: tiles?
cues.zh: 铺砌？

cues.en: Well, Robert Berger himself found a set with only a 104.
cues.zh: Robert Berger 本人就找到了一套只需 104 块的方案。

cues.en: Donald Knuth got the number down to 92 and then in 1969,
cues.zh: Donald Knuth 把数字降到了 92，然后在 1969 年，

cues.en: you had Rafael Robinson who came up with six tiles, just six that could tile the entire plane without ever repeating.
cues.zh: Rafael Robinson 提出了六块瓷砖，仅仅六块就能铺满整个平面且永不重复。

cues.en: Then along came Roger Penrose,
cues.zh: 接着 Roger Penrose 登场了，

cues.en: who would ultimately get the number down to two.
cues.zh: 他最终把数字降到了两块。

cues.en: Penrose started with a pentagon.
cues.zh: Penrose 从五边形开始。

cues.en: He added other pentagons around it and, of course, noticed the gaps. But this new shape could fit within a larger pentagon,
cues.zh: 他在它周围添加其他五边形，当然，注意到了空隙。但这个新形状可以嵌入一个更大的五边形中，

cues.en: which gave Penrose an idea. What if he took the original pentagons and broke them into smaller pentagons?
cues.zh: 这给了 Penrose 一个想法。如果他拿原来的五边形并把它们分成更小的五边形呢？

cues.en: Well, now some of the gaps start connecting up into rhombus shapes. Other gaps have three spikes.
cues.zh: 现在一些空隙开始连接成菱形。其他空隙有三个尖角。

cues.en: But Penrose didn't stop there. He subdivided the pentagons again.
cues.zh: 但 Penrose 没有止步于此。他再次细分五边形。

cues.en: Now some of the gaps are large enough that you can use pentagons to fill in part of them. And the remaining holes you're left with are just rhombuses,
cues.zh: 现在一些空隙足够大，可以用五边形填充其中一部分。剩下的孔洞就只有菱形、

cues.en: stars, and a fraction of a star that Penrose calls a justice cap.
cues.zh: 星形，以及 Penrose 称为“正义之帽”的星形的一部分。

cues.en: You can keep subdividing indefinitely,
cues.zh: 你可以无限地细分下去，

cues.en: and you will only ever find these shapes.
cues.zh: 而你只会发现这些形状。

cues.en: So with just these pieces, you can tile the plane aperiodically
cues.zh: 所以只用这些碎片，你就能非周期性地铺满平面

cues.en: with an almost fivefold symmetry.
cues.zh: 并具有近乎五重对称性。

cues.en: The fifth thing about Johannes Kepler is that if you take his pentagon pattern and you overlay it on top of Penrose's,
cues.zh: 关于约翰尼斯·开普勒的第五点是，如果你把他的五边形图案覆盖在彭罗斯的图案上，

cues.en: the two match up perfectly.
cues.zh: 这两者能够完美契合。

cues.en: Once Penrose had his pattern, he found ways to simplify the tiles.
cues.zh: 彭罗斯得到他的图案后，便开始寻找简化图块的方法。

cues.en: He distilled the geometry down to just two tiles, a thick rhombus and a thin rhombus.
cues.zh: 他将几何结构提炼为仅仅两种图块：一个宽菱形和一个窄菱形。

cues.en: The rules for how they can come together can be enforced by bumps and notches or by matching colors. And the rules ensure that these two single tiles can only tile the plane non periodically.
cues.zh: 它们组合的规则可以通过凸起与凹槽来强制执行，或者通过匹配颜色来约束。这些规则确保了这两个单一图块只能以非周期的方式铺满整个平面。

cues.en: Just two tiles go all the way out to infinity without ever repeating.
cues.zh: 仅仅两块图块就能无限延伸，且永不重复。

cues.en: Now one way to see this is to print up two copies of the same Penrose pattern
cues.zh: 现在，观察这一点的方法之一是打印出两份相同的彭罗斯图案，

cues.en: and one on a transparency
cues.zh: 其中一份印在透明胶片上，

cues.en: and overlay them on top of each other. Now the resulting interference you get is called a moire pattern.
cues.zh: 然后将它们重叠在一起。由此产生的干涉条纹被称为莫尔条纹。

cues.en: Where it is dark, the patterns are not aligned.
cues.zh: 在变暗的地方，图案没有对齐。

cues.en: We can see there are also some light spots and that's where the patterns do match up. And as I rotate around,
cues.zh: 我们可以看到也有一些亮点，那是图案契合的地方。当我旋转时，

cues.en: you can see the
cues.zh: 你可以看到

cues.en: light spots move in and get smaller, and then at a certain point, they move out
cues.zh: 亮点向内移动并变小，然后在某个特定点，它们向外移动

cues.en: and get bigger.
cues.zh: 并变大。

cues.en: And what I wanna do is try to enlarge
cues.zh: 我想做的是尝试放大

cues.en: one of these bright spots and see how big of a matching section I can find.
cues.zh: 其中一个亮点，看看能找到多大面积的匹配区域。

cues.en: Oh,
cues.zh: 哦，

cues.en: yes. Yes.
cues.zh: 太棒了。是的。

cues.en: It's like all of a sudden everything is illuminated.
cues.zh: 就像突然之间万物都被照亮了一样。

cues.en: I love it.
cues.zh: 我太喜欢了。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: these patterns are perfectly matching up here, here, here, here, and here, but not
cues.zh: 这些图案在这里、这里、这里、这里和这里都完美契合，但

cues.en: along these radial lines,
cues.zh: 沿着这些放射状的线条却没有，

cues.en: and that is why they look dark.
cues.zh: 这就是它们看起来很暗的原因。

cues.en: So what this shows us is that you can't ever match any section perfectly to one beneath it. There will always be some difference.
cues.zh: 这说明你永远无法让任何一个局部与下方的图块完美重合。总会有些差异。

cues.en: So my favorite Penrose pattern is actually made out of these two shapes,
cues.zh: 我最喜欢的彭罗斯图案其实是由这两种形状组成的，

cues.en: which are called kites
cues.zh: 分别叫做“风筝”

cues.en: and darts.
cues.zh: 和“飞镖”。

cues.en: And they have these very particular angles.
cues.zh: 它们有着非常特殊的角度。

cues.en: The way they're meant to match up is based on these two curves. You can see there's a curve on each piece.
cues.zh: 它们的拼接规则取决于这两条曲线。可以看到每片上面都有一段圆弧。

cues.en: And so you have to connect them so that the curves are continuous.
cues.zh: 拼接时必须让曲线保持连续。

cues.en: And that's the rule that allows you to build
cues.zh: 正是这条规则，能让你用这两片拼图

cues.en: an aperiodic tiling from these two pieces.
cues.zh: 拼出一种非周期性的密铺图案。

cues.en: So I laser cut
cues.zh: 于是我用激光切割了

cues.en: thousands
cues.zh: 数千块

cues.en: of these pieces and I'm gonna try to put them together and make a huge
cues.zh: 这样的拼图片，准备把它们拼在一起，做出一幅巨大的

cues.en: Penrose tiling.
cues.zh: 彭罗斯密铺。

cues.en: Oh, man.
cues.zh: 哎呀。

cues.en: Come on.
cues.zh: 拜托。

cues.en: If you stare at a pattern of kites and darts, you'll start to notice all kinds of regularities like stars and suns.
cues.zh: 如果你凝视图案中的风筝和飞镖，就会发现各种规律，比如星形和太阳形状。

cues.en: But look closer and they don't quite repeat in the way you'd expect them to.
cues.zh: 但再仔细看，它们并不会按你预想的方式重复出现。

cues.en: These two tiles create an ever changing pattern that extends out to infinity without repeating.
cues.zh: 这两种图元能拼出千变万化的图案，向外无限延伸且永不重复。

cues.en: Does this mean there is only one pattern of kites and darts
cues.zh: 这是否意味着风筝和飞镖拼成的图案其实只有这一种，

cues.en: and every picture that we see is just a portion of that overall
cues.zh: 我们见到的每一幅图，都只是整体中

cues.en: singular
cues.zh: 那个唯一的

cues.en: pattern?
cues.zh: 图案的一部分？

cues.en: Well, answer is no.
cues.zh: 答案其实是否定的。

cues.en: There are actually
cues.zh: 实际上，

cues.en: an uncountably
cues.zh: 存在着不可数

cues.en: infinite
cues.zh: 无穷多种

cues.en: number of different patterns of kites and darts that tile the entire plane.
cues.zh: 能够铺满整个平面的不同风筝与飞镖图案。

cues.en: And it gets weirder. If you were on any of those tilings,
cues.zh: 更神奇的是，如果你置身于其中任何一种密铺中，

cues.en: you wouldn't be able to tell which one it is. I mean, you might try to look further and further out, gather more and more data, but it's futile because
cues.zh: 你根本分辨不出自己在哪一种里面。就算你极目远眺、收集更多数据，也是徒劳的，因为

cues.en: any finite region of one of these tilings
cues.zh: 任何一种密铺中的任意有限区域，

cues.en: appears infinitely many times in all of the other versions of those tilings. I mean, don't get me wrong. Those tilings are also different in an infinite number of ways,
cues.zh: 都会在其他所有密铺版本中出现无穷多次。别误会，这些密铺彼此之间确实存在着无穷无尽的差异，

cues.en: but it's impossible to tell that unless you could see the whole pattern,
cues.zh: 但除非你能看到整个全局图案，否则根本无法分辨，

cues.en: which is impossible.
cues.zh: 而这又是根本不可能做到的。

cues.en: There's this kind of paradox to Penrose tilings where there's an uncountable
cues.zh: 彭罗斯拼贴存在这样一种悖论：有不可数个

cues.en: infinity
cues.zh: 无穷大

cues.en: of different versions,
cues.zh: 不同版本的，

cues.en: but just by looking at them, you could never tell them apart.
cues.zh: 但光看它们，你根本分辨不出来。

cues.en: Now, what if we count up all the kites and darts in this pattern?
cues.zh: 现在，如果我们把这个图案中的所有风筝形和飞镖形都数一数呢？

cues.en: Well, I get 440
cues.zh: 嗯，我得到的是 440

cues.en: kites and 272
cues.zh: 风筝和 272

cues.en: darts.
cues.zh: 飞镖。

cues.en: Does that ratio ring any bells? Well, if you divide one by the other, you get 1.618.
cues.zh: 这个比例听着耳熟吗？把两者相除，就得到 1.618。

cues.en: That is the golden ratio.
cues.zh: 这就是黄金比例。

cues.en: So why does the golden ratio appear in this pattern? Well, as you know, it contains a kind of fivefold symmetry.
cues.zh: 那么，为什么黄金比例会出现在这个图案中呢？如你所知，它含有一种五重对称性。

cues.en: And of all the irrational constants, the golden ratio phi
cues.zh: 而在所有无理常数中，黄金比例 $\phi$

cues.en: is the most of
cues.zh: 占据了绝大多数

cues.en: the constants. I mean, you can express the golden ratio as point five plus five to the power of point five times point five.
cues.zh: 就是常量。我的意思是，你可以把黄金比例表示为零点五加上五的零点五次方乘以零点五。

cues.en: The golden ratio is also heavily associated with pentagons. I mean, the ratio of the diagonal to an edge is the golden ratio. And the kite and dart pieces themselves are actually sections of pentagons,
cues.zh: 黄金比例也与五边形密切相关。我的意思是，对角线与边的比值就是黄金比例。而风筝和飞镖这两块本身就是五边形的部分，

cues.en: same with the rhombuses. So they actually have the golden ratio built right into their construction.
cues.zh: 菱形也一样。它们的构造中其实直接内置了黄金比例。

cues.en: The fact that the ratio of kites to darts approaches the golden ratio, an irrational number, provides evidence that the pattern can't possibly be periodic.
cues.zh: 风筝与飞镖的比例趋近于黄金比例这一无理数，这说明该模式不可能是周期性的。

cues.en: If the pattern were periodic, then the ratio of kites to darts could be expressed as a ratio of two whole numbers,
cues.zh: 如果图案是周期性的，那么风筝形与飞镖形的比例就可以表示为两个整数的比，

cues.en: the number of kites to darts in each periodic segment.
cues.zh: 每个周期段内风筝形与飞镖形数量的比值。

cues.en: And it goes deeper.
cues.zh: 而且它还要深奥。

cues.en: If you draw on the tiles, not curves,
cues.zh: 如果你在瓷砖上画的不是曲线，

cues.en: but these particular straight lines,
cues.zh: 而是这些特定的直线，

cues.en: well, now when you put the pattern together, you see something interesting.
cues.zh: 那么，现在当你把图案拼合在一起时，你会看到有趣的东西。

cues.en: They all connect up perfectly
cues.zh: 它们完美地连接在一起，

cues.en: into straight lines.
cues.zh: 形成了直线。

cues.en: There are five sets of parallel lines.
cues.zh: 有五组平行线。

cues.en: This is a kind of proof of the fivefold symmetry of the pattern.
cues.zh: 这可以说是对该图案五重对称性的一种证明。

cues.en: But it is not perfectly regular.
cues.zh: 但它并不是完全规则的。

cues.en: Take a look at any one set of parallel lines. You'll notice there are two different spacings, call them long and short.
cues.zh: 看看任意一组平行线。你会发现有两种不同的间距，姑且称它们为长和短。

cues.en: From the bottom, we have long, short, long, short, long, long.
cues.zh: 从底部开始，我们有长、短、长、短、长、长。

cues.en: Wait. That breaks the pattern.
cues.zh: 等等。这打破了规律。

cues.en: These gaps
cues.zh: 这些间隙

cues.en: don't follow a periodic pattern either.
cues.zh: 也不遵循周期性规律。

cues.en: But count up the number of longs and shorts in any section. Here, I get 13 shorts and 21 longs.
cues.zh: 但数一数任何区间里长和短的数量。这里，我得到了13个短的和21个长的。

cues.en: And you have the Fibonacci sequence.
cues.zh: 然后你就得到了斐波那契数列。

cues.en: One, one, two, three, five, eight, 13, 21, 34, and so on. And the ratio of one Fibonacci number to the previous one approaches
cues.zh: 一、一、二、三、五、八、13、21、34，以此类推。而且一个斐波那契数与前一个数的比值接近于

cues.en: the golden ratio.
cues.zh: 黄金分割率。

cues.en: Now the question Penrose faced from other scientists was, could there be a physical analogue for these patterns?
cues.zh: 现在，彭罗斯面临其他科学家的质疑是：这些图案会存在物理上的类似物吗？

cues.en: Do they occur in nature, perhaps in crystal structure?
cues.zh: 它们会自然出现吗，比如在晶体结构中？

cues.en: Penrose thought that was unlikely.
cues.zh: 彭罗斯认为这不太可能。

cues.en: The very nature of a crystal is that it is made up of repeating units, Just as the fundamental symmetries of the shapes that tile the plane had been worked out much earlier,
cues.zh: 晶体的本质就是由重复的单元组成的，正如铺满平面的形状的基本对称性很早就已被解开一样，

cues.en: the basic unit cells that compose all crystals were well established.
cues.zh: 组成所有晶体的基本晶胞已经得到了充分的确立。

cues.en: There are 14 of them, and no one had ever seen a crystal that failed to fit one of these patterns.
cues.zh: 一共有14种，而且从没有人见过不符合这些模式的晶体。

cues.en: And there was another problem. Crystals are built by putting atoms and molecules together locally.
cues.zh: 还有一个问题。晶体是通过在局部把原子和分子组合起来构建的。

cues.en: Whereas Penrose tilings, well, they seem to require some sort of long range coordination.
cues.zh: 而彭罗斯铺砌似乎需要某种长程协调。

cues.en: Take this pattern for example.
cues.zh: 以这个模式为例。

cues.en: You could put a dart
cues.zh: 你可以放一个飞镖

cues.en: over here and continue to tile out to infinity. No problems.
cues.zh: 在这里继续向无限延伸铺开。完全没问题。

cues.en: Or
cues.zh: 或者

cues.en: you could put a kite
cues.zh: 你可以放风筝

cues.en: over here on the other side. Again,
cues.zh: 在另一边这里。再说一次，

cues.en: no problems.
cues.zh: 没问题。

cues.en: But if you place
cues.zh: 但如果你放置

cues.en: the kite and dart in here simultaneously,
cues.zh: 这里同时存在风筝形和飞镖形瓷砖，

cues.en: well then this pattern will not work. I mean, you can keep tiling for a while,
cues.zh: 那么这种模式就行不通了。我的意思是，你可以继续平铺一段时间，

cues.en: but when you get to somewhere around here,
cues.zh: 但当你到达这里的某个地方时

cues.en: well, it's
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: not gonna work. You can put a dart in there, which completes the pattern nicely, but then you get this really awkward shape there,
cues.zh: 这样不行。你可以在那里加个省道，这样版型就完整了，但那里会形成一个很别扭的形状，

cues.en: which is actually the shape of another dart.
cues.zh: 这实际上是另一把飞镖的形状。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: if you put that one in there, then the lines don't match up. The pattern doesn't work. So how could this work as a crystal? I mean, both of these tiles obey the local rules,
cues.zh: 如果你把这个放进去，线条就对不上了。图案就不成立了。那这怎么能作为晶体成立呢？我是说，这两块瓷砖都遵守局部规则，

cues.en: but in the long term, they just don't work. In the early nineteen eighties, Paul Steinhardt and his students were using computers to model how atoms come together into condensed matter, that is essentially solid material at the smallest scales.
cues.zh: 但从长远来看，它们就是行不通。上世纪80年代初，Paul Steinhardt和他的学生们用计算机模拟原子如何结合成凝聚态物质，也就是最小尺度上的固体材料。

cues.en: And he found that locally they like to form icosahedrons.
cues.zh: 他发现它们在局部倾向于形成二十面体。

cues.en: But this was known to be the most forbidden shape because it is full of fivefold symmetries.
cues.zh: 但这种形状被认为是禁区中的禁区，因为它充满了五重对称性。

cues.en: So the question they posed was how big can these icosahedrons
cues.zh: 所以他们提出的问题是，这些二十面体

cues.en: get? They thought maybe 10 atoms or a 100 atoms.
cues.zh: 能有多大？他们以为也许是10个原子或100个原子。

cues.en: But inspired by Penrose tilings, they designed a new kind of structure, a three d analog of Penrose tilings now known as a quasicrystal.
cues.zh: 但受彭罗斯镶嵌的启发，他们设计了一种新结构，彭罗斯镶嵌的三维类似物，现在被称为准晶体。

cues.en: And they simulated how x rays would diffract off such a structure, and they found a pattern with rings of 10 points reflecting the fivefold symmetry.
cues.zh: 他们模拟了X射线如何在这种结构上衍射，结果发现了一个带有10个点环的图案，反映出五重对称性。

cues.en: Just a few 100 kilometers away, completely unaware of their work, another scientist, Dan Schechtman,
cues.zh: 就在几百公里外，另一位科学家Dan Schechtman完全不知道他们的工作，

cues.en: created this flaky material from aluminum and manganese.
cues.zh: 用铝和锰制造出了这种片状材料。

cues.en: And when he scattered electrons off his material,
cues.zh: 当他让电子在自己的材料上散射时，

cues.en: this is the picture he got.
cues.zh: 这就是他得到的图像。

cues.en: It almost perfectly
cues.zh: 它几乎完美地

cues.en: matches the one made by Steinhardt.
cues.zh: 匹配了Steinhardt做出的那个。

cues.en: So if Penrose tilings require
cues.zh: 那么，如果彭罗斯镶嵌需要

cues.en: long range coordination,
cues.zh: 长程协调，

cues.en: then how do you possibly make quasicrystals?
cues.zh: 你又怎么可能制造出准晶体呢？

cues.en: Well, I was talking to Paul Steinhardt about this and he told me, if you just use the matching rules on the edges,
cues.zh: 嗯，我和Paul Steinhardt聊过这件事，他告诉我，如果你只在边上使用匹配规则，

cues.en: those rules are not strong enough. And if you apply them locally, you run into problems like this. You misplace
cues.zh: 那些规则不够强。如果你在局部应用它们，就会遇到这样的问题。你会放错

cues.en: tiles.
cues.zh: 瓦片。

cues.en: But he said, if you have rules for the vertices, the way the vertices connect connect with each other, those rules are strong enough locally so that you never make a mistake, and the pattern can go on to infinity.
cues.zh: 但他说，如果你有关于顶点的规则，也就是顶点之间如何连接，那些规则在局部足够强，所以你永远不会犯错，图案可以一直延伸到无穷。

cues.en: One of the seminal papers on quasicrystals
cues.zh: 准晶体领域的开创性论文之一

cues.en: was called Deniva quinquangula
cues.zh: 叫做《论五边形

cues.en: on the pentagonal
cues.zh: 雪花》

cues.en: snowflake,
cues.zh: (Deniva quinquangula)，

cues.en: in a shout out to Kepler.
cues.zh: 这是在向开普勒致敬。

cues.en: Now not everyone was delighted at the announcement of quasicrystals,
cues.zh: 然而，并不是所有人都对准晶体的宣布感到高兴，

cues.en: a material that up until then people thought totally defied the laws of nature.
cues.zh: 这是一种在此之前人们认为完全违背自然规律的材料。

cues.en: Double Nobel Prize winner Linus Pauling famously remarked,
cues.zh: 双料诺贝尔奖得主莱纳斯·鲍林曾有一句名言：

cues.en: there are no quasi crystals,
cues.zh: 世上没有准晶体，

cues.en: only quasi scientists.
cues.zh: 只有准科学家。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但

cues.en: Schechtman got the last laugh. He was awarded the Nobel Prize for chemistry in 2011.
cues.zh: 谢赫特曼笑到了最后。他被授予了2011年诺贝尔化学奖。

cues.en: And quasicrystals have since been grown with beautiful dodecahedral
cues.zh: 自那以后，人们已经培育出了具有美丽十二面体

cues.en: shapes.
cues.zh: 形状的准晶体。

cues.en: They are currently being explored for applications from nonstick electrical insulation and cookware to ultra durable steel.
cues.zh: 目前，人们正在探索它们在不粘电绝缘材料、炊具到超耐用钢材等领域的应用。

cues.en: And the thing about this whole story that fascinates me the most is what exists that we just can't perceive because it's considered impossible.
cues.zh: 整个故事中最让我着迷的是，有哪些事物因为被认为是不可能的，而我们根本无法感知？

cues.en: I mean, the symmetries of regular geometric shapes seemed so obvious and certain that no one thought to look beyond them. That is until Penrose.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，规则几何形状的对称性显得如此明显和确定，以至于没有人想到要去超越它们去寻找。直到彭罗斯出现。

cues.en: And what we found are patterns that are both beautiful and counterintuitive,
cues.zh: 而我们发现的图案既美观又反直觉，

cues.en: and materials that existed all along that we just couldn't see for what they really are.
cues.zh: 还有那些一直存在、而我们只是无法看清其庐山真面目的材料。
